**Finding submitted: `missing` (INSURANCE), confidence 0.90**

**What I found:** The Agreement has no insurance provision at all — a full-text search for "insurance" returned zero results, and the section outline confirms no insurance heading exists among Sections 1–30.

**Why it matters here:**
- TrueLink is a hosting vendor that hosts our Web Site, operates the Interface, and transmits Client Content and consumer credit data — squarely within the playbook's "processes Customer Data" trigger.
- TrueLink's liability for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 is already capped at 12 months of hosting/support fees (p0077), and it gives a mutual indemnity in Section 12(b) — neither is backed by any coverage requirement.
- This falls close to the walk-away line (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data), so the preferred position is proportionate rather than aggressive.

**Redline (validated `ok:true`):** Inserted a new **Section 31 (Insurance)** immediately after Section 30 (Force Majeure), the last substantive miscellaneous provision and just ahead of the signature blocks:

- CGL: USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate
- Professional liability (E&O): USD 2,000,000
- Cyber liability: USD 5,000,000 (tied to TrueLink's processing of Client Content and consumer data)
- Workers' compensation as required by law
- Certificates of insurance on request; term plus one year

**Direction check:** The obligation runs against the counterparty only and imposes nothing on us. The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if the limits meet resistance.

**One item worth flagging for your review:** the survival clause (p0090) covers "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so a new Section 31 would sit outside it. I deliberately left that alone to keep the edit minimal, since the new clause carries its own express duration ("throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter"). If you would rather belt-and-braces it, extending that reference to "5 through 31" is a trivial follow-on edit.
